judgments.reasoning_cat1: It refers to arbitrators 'listed in Section 16-E. 1' when the list is actually compiled under 16-E.2, and the availability trigger ('within thirty days after his selection') presupposes a selection that has failed.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: 16-E.2 is the list-making provision and 16-E.1(a) the selection provision, so the internal cross-reference does not match the structure of the section.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The final sentence directs replacement 'by the procedures of 16-E. 2. above' inside 16-E.2 itself, a circular self-reference.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: 16-E.1 refers to 'the list compiled in accordance with 16-E. 2' while 16-E.3 calls it 'the existing list ... in paragraph 16-E. 1', so the section is inconsistent about where the list lives.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Both parties shall have the right to strike up to five arbitrators' from a fifteen-name list could leave five or ten names, and the clause locates the list in the wrong paragraph.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: 16-E.2 is the list-making provision, so the reference to 'paragraph 16-E. 1' repeats the mismatch found in 16-E.1(b).

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'The chairman and any two other members' as a quorum for a five-member board permits decisions by two partisans plus the chairman; stated plainly but with a corrupted word ('quo1em').
judgments.reasoning_cat2: 16-K speaks of 'a majority' of the Board making awards, which does not sit easily with a three-member quorum of a five-member body.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'The permanent impartial chairmen designated under Section 16-M' is plural and uses 'permanent' for officers whose terms 16-M.1 makes annual.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: 16-M.1 provides for a new Impartial Chairman each year and the Status Quo Arbitrator letter provides for holdover service beyond expiration, which conflicts with termination 'upon the expiration of this Agreement'.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Exclusive jurisdiction over any issue arising with regard to the provisions of Section 4-A' is broad but precisely bounded.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: 4-H directs questions on the interpretation or application of those very provisions to the Joint Standing Committee and/or Appeals Board — a direct conflict with exclusivity.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A broad rule-making power with a no-record default, stated plainly.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: 16-E.1(a) requires the Appeals Board to proceed under rules 'adopted by the Union and the Publishers' Association', which is a different rule-making source.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A precise default-appearance rule with a three-day notice period.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: 16-P allows all Section 16 time limits to be extended by mutual agreement; consistent.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Shall include, but shall not be limited to' following a list of specific remedies is the classic general-after-specific construction, and 'other person' extends the protected class without definition.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: 13-G caps shortage relief at one-half of one per cent and 16-M.4 prescribes a specific restore-the-status-quo remedy, both of which limit this otherwise unbounded power.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A short waiver of oath requirements; it omits the Appeals Board chairman from the list of those covered by the second half.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: 16-E and 16-M provide for the impartial chairman and arbitrators, who are only partly covered here; a minor gap.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The annual terms, the March 31–March 30 service year and the twenty-one day fallback are all stated with precision.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: 16-G says the term of the 'permanent' impartial chairmen ends with the Agreement, and the Status Quo Arbitrator letter has the incumbents hold over until replaced.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The parenthetical exception for 'a period which the parties mutually declare to be a temporary period' is workable, though it depends on a joint declaration that may never be made.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: 16-M.5 makes the chairman selected under 16-M.1 and 16-M.2 the fifth member for change-of-conditions cases; consistent.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'No change in condition' is the contract's broadest undefined phrase, and the exception cross-refers to 'Section 8-D' when the layoff provision is 3-D.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: 3-D.1 and 3-B give the Publisher unilateral rights to rearrange routes and set delivery methods, and 6-E empowers the foreman to make changes in operating procedures, all of which strain against a consent requirement.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The thirty-day pivot is precise, but the clause gives the Union alone the right to seek restoration and the printed figures are corrupted as '(80) days'.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: 16-M.3 says either party may demand a hearing, so the asymmetry here is unexplained; the Changed Conditions memorandum adds a further interpretive layer.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The final sentence is corrupted and the limitation — the Board 'may only hear and decide the merits of the underlying grievances ... with the consent of both parties' — is awkwardly expressed.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: 16-E.1 provides a different fifth-member selection for all other matters, and 16-A's general channel does not contemplate this bifurcation.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Or other cessation of work or interference therewith' is a general phrase after two specifics, and the exception permits self-help against a non-complying party.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The News Memorandum of Understanding ¶3 refers to 'the provisions against strikes and disruptions of orderly relationships', a formulation broader than this clause.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A plain equal-sharing rule for arbitral fees.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: 21-F.1 makes The News pay all actuary costs and 22-C.e sends relief disputes to a named individual without a fee rule; minor asymmetries only.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A one-line extension provision; unambiguous.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It softens 16-A's 30-day waiver and 16-C's two-week deadline consistently.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: It reprints an entire former clause 'in italics for reference only and not as a part of this Agreement', yet the reprinted text is partly corrupted and partly identical to operative 2-L.3.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: 2-L.1 says union security exists 'to the extent embodied in Section 17', and 17-A.2 would automatically restore the italicized text, so the operative content of the union-security scheme is genuinely uncertain.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The trigger reads 'if any provision as shown above in italics ... no longer is held to be inoperative', a double negative that inverts the evident intent and leaves the condition unclear.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: 17-A.1 declares the italicized text is not part of the Agreement, while this clause makes it automatically part of it on a contingency, and 2-L.1 measures union security by 'Section 17'.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A long but conventional separability mechanism with a defined trigger, a defined consequence and a renegotiation right.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: 4-A.5 provides a narrower conformity rule for hiring procedures and 13-A.5 gives the Union a termination right on wage controls, so three different responses to legal interference coexist.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'The spirit as well as the letter' invites a standard outside the text, and 'renders impossible or inoperative any provisions' is broad.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: 3-M expressly contemplates the parties agreeing with third parties to different terms, and 17-B contemplates provisions becoming inoperative, both of which sit against this promise.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A short zipper clause, though the text is corrupted ('they have argained') and the heading is separated from the body.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: 20-B, 21-G.2, 5-L and several letters commit the parties to further bargaining during the term, which cuts against a settled-for-the-term clause.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Merger, consolidation, or permanent suspension' and the eight-week (40 shift) measure are stated precisely, though 'any other money due them' is open-ended.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: 12-D.1(3)(e) caps a Publisher's suspension and merger pay liability for wholesaler employees at 15 days, and 4-A.2(b) treats the same events as Group 1 listing triggers.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The dual character — a single instrument to be 'treated ... as an individual agreement between them' — is a real conceptual tension stated in one sentence.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The preamble makes the Association agent for both Publishers and binds successors, and Sections 21 and 22 contain separate shop conditions for each paper, so the individual/collective character runs through the whole document.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The notice mechanism is clear but the internal deadline is printed as 'thirty (36) days', and the mediation step is permissive and mutual.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Subparagraph (b) explains the 75-day figure by reference to a 65-day alternative that appears nowhere else in the instrument.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: It is explanatory rather than operative — 'is in the hope that' creates no obligation — and refers to a 65-day period not used elsewhere.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: This is a recital-style gloss sitting inside the operative termination section, and its stated purpose (agreement two weeks before expiry) is not enforced by (a).

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Pay at his normal straight-time weekly pay' for daily leave days is a unit mismatch, and the second sentence uses a different measure ('the rate he receives for the majority of his shifts') for the same payment.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: 13-K.2 prices unused and accumulated leave 'at the then prevailing rate' and requires cash payment in December, which is a third measure for the same entitlement.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: An agreement to undertake a joint study 'to define the types of clerical work which are appropriate' — the substantive question is expressly left open.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: 2-A.1 and 2-B already purport to fix unit coverage and 13-C prices non-covered work, so deferring the definition of clerical work leaves those clauses incomplete.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Overtime which would normally be assigned to employees who are paid a higher rate' turns on an unstated norm.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: 5-M requires overtime to be worked as the employer requires and gives a complaint route for unfair distribution, which this clause narrows without saying how the two interact.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The parenthetical '(discounting the vacation period before or after the holiday)' is opaque, and the proviso giving the Foreman discretion contradicts the same sentence's use of seniority.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It routes holiday pay 'in accordance with Section 13-B. 4', a vacation clause, when eligibility is set by 7-D, and 13-B.2(a) already fixes vacation scheduling by seniority at the employer's convenience.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Notwithstanding any provision to the contrary' is a blanket override whose displaced provisions are not identified, and 'eliminate, reduce or phase-out' bundles three different events.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It expressly overrides the rest of the Agreement, and 20-E.6 then disapplies Sections 3 and 4 to a subset of men, so the interaction with 3-D and Section 4 must be worked out from outside the clause.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A bare written-notice requirement with no time period specified.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The Thirty Days Notice memorandum requires 30 days' notice of any major operational change, which supplies a period this clause omits.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The protection is conditioned on the situation 'having been designated as an excess situation', so the Publisher's own designation controls the benefit.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: 20-E.6 carves out holders aged seventy or more from the no-layoff promise, and 3-D.1 preserves the general layoff right, so the guarantee is qualified twice over.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'No longer required because of such elimination, reduction or phasing-out' is a causal test left to the Publisher's designation.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: 3-D.5 uses the same 'excess' concept for automation with a two-week determination requirement absent here.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The parenthetical '(so that an additional situation is not made)' explains the mechanism clearly.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: 4-B requires vacancies to be posted for four weeks and filled by regular situation holders by seniority, and 20-E.5(a) displaces that ordering entirely.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Other available work described in Section 2 ... for which they are qualified' is broad but anchored to an enumerated list.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: 2-I bars discharge for inability to perform some other operation, and 4-A.4 requires competence; consistent in direction.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The final clause — 'except as to excess situation holders who are seventy (70) or more years of age nor shall the provisions of Sections 3 and 4 of the Agreement be applicable to them' — has an ambiguous antecedent for 'them' and disapplies two whole sections without saying to what end.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Disapplying Sections 3 and 4 removes the layoff-notice and seniority protections of 4-E and the review right in 3-D.1 for an unidentified group, which cannot be squared with those provisions.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Or that portion of it hereby affected' is vague, and the discretion over starting times and days off is stated without limit.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: 5-J requires four days' notice of starting-time and day-off changes with a penalty, and Supplementary Agreement ¶4 guarantees named Times holders against any change, both of which this clause overrides only by implication.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'The Times will continue its present practice' leaves one party's obligation entirely undefined while the other's is precise.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 19 treats this as an individual agreement with each Publisher, which explains the asymmetry; no square conflict.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Questions ... which are subject to arbitration under the contract and which are submitted to arbitration will be arbitrated under Section 16' is circular and adds nothing that Section 16 does not already say.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: 16-A already channels all interpretation disputes to the same machinery, so this clause is either redundant or implies some questions are not arbitrable.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'What are currently known as' fixes the sections by an undated present-tense reference, and the geographic split is stated with care.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: 21-B.4 declares this all-advertising-sections agreement ended effective March 30, 1975, which makes its presence in a 1981-84 contract hard to explain.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A precise negative covenant tied to three named holidays.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: 21-B.4 terminates this whole arrangement as of March 30, 1975, yet the Continuation of Side Agreements memorandum says every side agreement is continued and 'deemed updated'.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The alternating nine-month/three-month schedule is intricate but stated, and all the dates fall in 1974-75.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: 21-B.4 ends the arrangement in 1975 while the Continuation memorandum purports to continue and update every side agreement, leaving the status of these lapsed periods unresolved.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A single sentence fixing an end date, with the subject supplied only by a bracketed editorial insertion.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: An agreement stated to end in 1975 is reproduced as an operative provision of a 1981-84 contract, and the Continuation memorandum deems every side agreement continued and updated — a direct incoherence.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The trigger is a list of copy counts ('75, 60, 50, 40 or fewer copies per load') plus alternative conditions joined by 'or ... or when both conditions exist', which is hard to parse, and it names four individuals.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: 5-M and 20-C govern overtime assignment generally, and guaranteed overtime for four named men fits awkwardly with 8-C's non-discrimination rule on overtime distribution.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A precise page-count trigger and load cap with one named exception.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: 21-D.I sets different maximum loads for Newspoint routes and 3-A.2 requires each Publisher to publish load schedules, so several load caps operate at once.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Eight lettered points of very different character are bundled together; (b)'s 'no reduction in the present number of a.m. routes' is undated and (d) commits only to send a letter agreeing to meet.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Point (g)'s 180-load tailman rule is expressly subject to the Newspoint Agreement, whose 21-D schedules use quite different thresholds, and (b) cuts against 3-D.1's route-reduction right.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Transport men hired according to need' is a fragment that states no ascertainable obligation.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: 4-A.2 governs hiring order from the shape lists, which 'according to need' does not acknowledge.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The table's column heading is 'Maximum Number of Loads with o Tailmen' while the closing sentence says tailmen will be employed on all runs under the schedule, and the papers-per-load column runs 150, 100, 45, 50, 40 out of order.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: 21-C.3(g) uses a flat 180-load tailman trigger 'except as provided in the Newspoint Agreement', and Schedules B and C set different numbers, so several tailman rules apply to the same trucks.
